evidence: Cic. Cael. 17: in aediculīs habitat (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Where one lives goes in the locative (Rhodī, Rōmae, rūrī) or with in and the ablative; with whom, cum or apud (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Att. 14.20.4: vīvit habitatque cum Balbō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of the life one leads in a place: Rhodī vīvere (Cic. Fam. 4.7.4, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Caes. BG 1.1.1: quārum ūnam incolunt Belgae
terms.comment: Of a people and its country; in Cicero always with an accusative (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Samia mihi māter fuit: ea habitābat Rhodī.
phrases.english: My mother came from Samos; she lived on Rhodes.

phrases.latin: Ubi habitat? — Nē id quidem. — Ubi vīdistī? — In viā.
phrases.english: Where does she live? — I don’t even know that. — Where did you see her? — In the street.

phrases.latin: nōs enim ita philologī sumus ut vel cum fabrīs habitāre possīmus
phrases.english: for we are such scholars that we could even live with the builders in the house

sources: Lewis & Short: habito · Lewis & Short: vivo · Lewis & Short: incolo
